 JUDGMENT Parents of Srihari filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 alleging that on 01.03.2020 at 8.15 a.m., when Srihari was riding Bike bearing No.KA-05-JR-0302 by keep sitting Madhu on the pillion from Bengaluru towards Chickaballapur on NH- 44, near Siddalaghatta Flyover, the driver of Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 negligently abruptly parked the same in the middle of the road without providing signal/parking lights, thereby made the Bike to dash to the rear part of the Heavy Goods Vehicle resulting in instantaneous death of Srihari.
2. As on the date of accident, Srihari being aged about 26 years, used to earn Rs.60,000/- p.m. with annual bonus and arrears of Rs.50,000/- by working as Software Engineer/QA Engineer at Popreach Technologies Private Limited, Vasanth Nagar, Bengaluru.
3. Regarding the accident Chickaballapur Traffic police registered a case in crime No.12/2020.
4. Inspite of service of the notice, respondent No.1 owner of Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company appeared through his advocate, filed written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age,
occupation and income of the deceased.
In para No.2 (j) of the written statement respondent No.2 asserted that due to the sole negligent riding of the Bike bearing No.KA-05-JR-0302 by the deceased, the accident taken place.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 21.04.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 01.03.2020 at about 8.15 to 8.20 a.m., on Siddlaghatta Flyover, Bengaluru- K.N. Mukthamani vs Amar Singh on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5262407/
2 Chickaballapura NH-44 road, Chickaballapura, Karnataka, the death caused to one Srihari Y.G., was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Goods Vehicle bearing Reg. No.MH-34/AV-8192 as alleged?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
petitioner No.2-Y.Gururaju deposed as P.W.1 and produced 18 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.18.

On 21.11.2024 petitioner produced the evidence of Police Inspector, Chickaballapura traffic police station as P.W.2.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.
On 28.01.2025 the counsel for the petitioners filed the written arguments.

9. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... Due to the negligent use of the Bike bearing No.KA-05-JR-0302 by Srihari, negligent use of Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 by Sumith, S/o.Jaisingh at the ratio of 50:50 accident taken place resulting in the death of Srihari.
Issue No.2 ...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.21,80,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order  for the following:-

on 01.03.2020 at 8.15 to 8.20 a.m.
when Srihari was riding Bike bearing No.KA-05-JR-0302 by keep sitting Madhu on the pillion from Bengaluru towards Chickaballapur on NH- 44, near Siddalaghatta Flyover, driver of Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 negligently abruptly parked the same in the middle of the road in a negligent manner endangering to human life without any parking lights, indications, thereby made the Bike to dash to the rear part of the Heavy Goods Vehicle resulting instantaneous death of Srihari.

11. In the written statement respondent No.2 - Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident and asserted that due to the sole negligent riding of Bike by Srihari, the accident taken place.

15. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.12/2020 registered by Chickaballapur traffic police against Sumit, S/o.Jaysingh, driver of Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192,
Srihari Y.G., rider of Bike bearing No.KA-05-JR-0302 for having committed the offence punishable under Sections 379, 283, 304-A of IPC, on 01.03.2020 at 8.15 a.m., resulting in the death of Srihari and Madhu H.M.

16. In this case, there are no evidence to disbelieve the contents of the police records, evidence of P.W.1, P.W.2 regarding reason, mode of accident and consequence of the accident.

17. Hence, I have concluded that on 01.03.2020 at 08.15 a.m. on Bengaluru - Chickaballapur NH-44,
near Siddalaghatta Flyover, due to the negligent use of Bike bearing No.KA-05-JR-0302 by Srihari and negligent use of Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 by Sumit at the ratio of 50:50, the Bike dashed to rear part of the Heavy Goods Vehicle, thereby accident taken place resulting in the death of Srihari.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 accordingly.

P.W.1 admitted that as per Ex.P.17-TDS Traces Form No.29AS for the assessment year 2020-21, the total taxable income of the deceased was Rs.4,83,326/- p.a.

22. In the copy of D.L. marked at Ex.P.15, date of birth of the deceased Srihari is noted as 14.09.1993.
In the copy of Income tax returns for the assessment year 2019- 20, the income of the deceased is noted as Rs.4,04,479/-.

In the Form No.16 for the period from 1.04.2019 to 31.03.2020,
total income, deductions towards income tax and income after deductions of tax of Srihari are noted as Rs.6,81,990/-, Rs.1,03,262 and Rs.5,78,728/- respectively.

23. In this case petitioners have not produced documentary evidence regarding quantum of income of deceased Srihari for the period of three years immediately prior to 01.03.2020 i.e., the date of accident.

In this case, there is no dispute regarding education qualification of Srihari as on the date of accident.
24.
Copy of Aadhar card shows that petitioners are the parents of deceased Srihari.

Hence, I have calculated compensation under the head of loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Srihari as on the 27 years date of accident :
Average annual income of Srihari as on Rs.5,00,000/- the date of incident:
Less: 50% towards personal expenses: Rs.2,50,000/- (Rs. 5,00,000/- -
Rs.2,50,000/-) Annual income of the deceased: Rs.2,50,000/-
Loss of dependency Rs.2,50,000 x 17: Rs.42,50,000/-
25.

Hence, I assessed compensation under the head of Loss of Dependency at Rs.42,50,000/-,
Rs.15,000/- under the head of loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- under the head of funeral expenses,
Rs.80,000/- under the head of loss of consortium to the petitioners No.1 and 2 at the rate of Rs.40,000/- each.

In the written statement respondent No.2 admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 as on the date of incident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident, respondent No.1-owner of the Heavy Goods Vehicle has violated any terms of the policy.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that theo respondents being the owner and insurer of the Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No. No.MH-34/AV-8192 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents being the owner and insurer of the Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.21,80,000/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Heavy Goods Vehicle bearing No.MH-34/AV-8192 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation and interest may be released to the petitioners by crediting the same to their bank accounts directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
